title: Tolerance to postoperative refractive error of the TECNIS PureSee™ IOL
summary:
In cataract surgery, the eye’s natural, clouded lens is removed and replaced with an artificial lens. In most cases, a monofocal lens is implanted; however, this usually results in a dependence on glasses (mostly for near vision). 
Although multifocal lenses offer the advantage of potentially enabling glasses-free vision, this is usually accompanied by increased optical side effects such as glare, halos, or loss of contrast sensitivity. The TECNIS PureSee™ IOL was developed to achieve a high level of independence from glasses while minimizing optical side effects. This study examines how well this goal is achieved and to what extent postoperative refractive errors influence dependence on glasses.

interventions.name: Bilateral implantation of the TECNIS PureSee™ or TECNIS PureSee™ toric intraocular lens during cataract surgery

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Men/Women 
- 18 years of age or older 
- Bilateral cataracts requiring surgery 
- Endothelial cells (EC)/mm² > 2,000 EC/mm² (in both eyes) 
- Expected postoperative visual acuity of 100% (in both eyes), defined by the presence of a healthy cornea and retina appropriate for the patient’s age
Exclusion criteria:
- Expected postoperative astigmatism >0.75 dpt. 
- Irregular astigmatism 
- Pupil diameter < 5 mm 
- Inability to attend follow-up examinations for health or social reasons 
- Corneal diseases that impair visual acuity (including Fuchs’ endothelial dystrophy, corneal decompensation, central corneal scars) 
- Retinal diseases that impair visual acuity (including age-related macular diseases, cystoid macular edema, macular scars)
